definition: delay or prevent something bad from happening
memoryTip: Hold off danger with a stave (staff) — keep the bad thing at bay.
correctPassage: Extra funding helped the clinic stave off closure for another year.
wrongPassages: The chef hoped to stave off dinner by plating the first course early.
She staved off the award ceremony by accepting the trophy with a speech.
Volunteers staved off the festival by opening the gates an hour ahead of schedule.

definition: make happen sooner or more quickly
memoryTip: Think expedition: speed the process so it arrives sooner.
correctPassage: The clerk offered to expedite the passport renewal for travelers leaving Friday.
wrongPassages: Managers decided to expedite the project by adding three more months to the deadline.
He expedited the argument by refusing to reply for weeks.
They expedited the meal by letting it cool on the counter all afternoon.

definition: rate at which people leave and are replaced; or total sales
memoryTip: Staff or stock turns over — how fast people/goods cycle through.
correctPassage: Low turnover kept the research team stable through the multi-year study.
wrongPassages: The coach praised the team's turnover for never swapping players mid-season.
She measured the room's turnover as the distance from wall to wall.
His turnover for the night meant he slept through every alarm.

memoryTip: Stifle a yawn or a fire — smother it so it cannot break free.
correctPassage: Strict rules can stifle creativity when every idea needs three approvals.
wrongPassages: The coach hoped to stifle the players by giving them freer practice drills.
Open debate stifled the bill by bringing every amendment to a full vote.
She stifled the engine so it would roar louder on the highway.

definition: withdraw a former statement or belief
memoryTip: Re-cant: sing the claim again the other way — take it back.
correctPassage: Facing new evidence, the witness agreed to recant her earlier testimony.
wrongPassages: He recanted the hymn by singing the first verse louder than before.
The mayor recanted her support by repeating the same endorsement on TV.
Students recanted the lecture notes into a cleaner outline for class.

definition: easy to control, manage, or influence
memoryTip: Tractable like a tract you can handle — easy to manage or solve.
correctPassage: Once simplified, the math problem became tractable for most of the class.
wrongPassages: The wild horse was tractable only after it threw every rider who tried.
Her tractable schedule left no room for last-minute changes of any kind.
Engineers called the crash tractable because the wreckage filled three lanes.

correctPassage: Climbing the ridge in a storm would be perilous even for experts.
wrongPassages: The babysitter called the quiet nap room perilous for the sleeping twins.
A perilous commute meant empty roads and green lights the whole way home.
Tourists preferred the perilous boardwalk because every railing was new.

memoryTip: Ex-asperate: push past the last of someone's patience.
correctPassage: Endless hold music began to exasperate customers waiting for support.
wrongPassages: The nurse hoped to exasperate the pain with a carefully chosen sedative.
Soft lighting and calm music exasperated the spa guests into deep rest.
She exasperated the deadline by finishing the report two days early.

definition: speak or write about someone in an abusively critical way
memoryTip: Turn someone into a villain with harsh, smearing words.
correctPassage: Critics tried to vilify the scientist instead of addressing her data.
wrongPassages: The host planned to vilify the guest by praising every career highlight.
Editors vilified the draft by adding only minor grammar fixes.
She vilified the charity by donating anonymously every month.

memoryTip: Like congruent triangles — same shape, in agreement.
correctPassage: Her actions were congruent with the values she taught her students.
wrongPassages: The two reports were congruent: one predicted growth, the other collapse.
His congruent alibi conflicted with every camera timestamp on file.
The committee called the plans congruent after rejecting half the agenda.
